newsitem.title: USA: Accused Fla. man may have killed in Texas - police.
newsitem.headline: Accused Fla. man may have killed in Texas - police.

text.p: Two Florida sisters whom police believe were killed by a "sexual predator" were buried on Tuesday as officials investigated whether their accused killer might be behind the death of a Texas girl who became a national symbol of child sex abuse.
Hundreds of people, many of whom did not know the girls, attended the funeral for Alicia Sybilla Jones, 7, and DeAnn Emerald Mu-min, 11, of Oakland Park, Fla.
The girls' bodies were found on Wednesday in the attic of the home of Howard Steven Ault, their suspected kidnapper and killer, police said.

Ault, who had a record of sexual attacks against children, had been classified by the judicial system as a "sexual predator" before he was charged with the sisters' deaths. He also was charged with sexual assault on the older girl.
Ault had just been jailed on a child sex charge involving a Dec. 31, 1995, attack on an 11-year-old girl, when police identified him as the chief suspect in the latest killings.
He had been under house arrest for another attack on a young girl when he was arrested in connection with the assault on the 11-year-old.

Fort Lauderdale police on Tuesday were investigating a possible Texas connection to their case. Detectives from Florida had travelled to Arlington, Texas, to look into whether Ault might be linked to the abduction and death in January of 9-year-old Amber Hagerman, whose body was discovered near where Ault may have been staying.

Hagerman became a national symbol of child sexual abuse and her parents appealed to Congress to establish a national database for convicted sex offenders to help track down those who move from state to state. In September, Congress passed the Amber Hagerman Child Protection Act, which mandates tough penalties for repeat child sex offenders.

Police recovered Ault's pickup truck in Texas and said they believed that Ault's wife might have driven the truck to her mother's house there the day after the girls were killed. But they have not yet found any evidence showing Ault was in Texas at the time of Amber Hagerman's murder.

"That is what they are focusing on right now," Arlington police spokesman Dee Anderson said. "We have followed thousands of leads and checked out thousands of people, and this is just one more at this point."

Alicia and DeAnn's murders have outraged southern Florida. The yard of Ault's home has been turned into an informal shrine to the girls and an angry public has demanded explanations for why Ault was not jailed far earlier.
